Pause a container inside a try block with a finally unpause, or use withPausedContainer.

nitpicker/contract-infrastructure-type.description: Keep persistence handles and request or response objects out of the exports of a feature index
messages: Take a repository or a port interface and return a domain type or a plain record from {{member}}: {{type}} from {{package}} is a persistence handle, so every importer of feature {{feature}} depends on its database session. Keep {{type}} in the feature's adapters behind the index; a factory (a function that returns an object synchronously) that receives it from the composition root is fine. An exception fits only when the feature deliberately hands out the handle, such as a shared transaction helper.

Take plain values and return a domain type or a plain record from {{member}}: {{type}} from {{package}} is a request or response object, so every importer of feature {{feature}} needs a live HTTP exchange. Read it in the route handler and pass the values in. An exception fits only when the export is a route handler or middleware the framework calls with a different first parameter.

nitpicker/exhaustive-union-predicate.description: Disallow classifying a union by listing only some of its members
messages: These comparisons list only some members of {{ union }}, so a member added later is silently classified as the default. Classify every member with a `switch` that has no `default`, or a `Record<Union, boolean>` lookup, so adding a member fails to compile.

nitpicker/fake-timers-require-restore.description: Require fake timers, and stubs made in test files, to be restored
messages: Fake timers stay on for the tests that follow. Restore them: `afterEach(() => { vi.useRealTimers(); });`.

Fake timers stay on for the tests that follow. Restore them: `afterEach(() => { vi.useRealTimers(); });`. With user-event, create the user with `userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers: vi.advanceTimersByTime })` or its clicks wait forever.
This stubbed global stays stubbed for the tests that follow. Restore it: `afterEach(() => { vi.unstubAllGlobals(); });`, or stub it once in a setup file.
This stubbed environment variable stays set for the tests that follow. Restore it: `afterEach(() => { vi.unstubAllEnvs(); });`.

nitpicker/file-name-casing.description: Name files in the one casing the project's files already use
messages: File name "{{name}}" is not {{casing}}, which this project uses for file names. Rename it, pin a different casing with "conventions": { "typescript.fileNames": "camelCase" } in nitpicker.config.json. An exception fits only when the name is deliberate.
File name "{{name}}" is not {{casing}}, which most other files in this folder use. Rename it. An exception fits only when the name is deliberate.

nitpicker/handler-entity-type.description: Keep ORM entities out of route handler signatures and response bodies
messages: Take and return a plain record (DTO) in {{site}} and map {{entity}} to it in the service: {{entity}} is a {{orm}} entity, so the response serializes every column and loaded relation and ties the API to the database schema. An exception fits only when the entity is deliberately the API model, such as a read-only projection.

Run git in tests with a hermetic environment: pass an `env` object, written in this file, that sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL (for example to '/dev/null') and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, so the developer's global git config (commit signing, hooks) does not apply.

nitpicker/integration-test-uses-approved.description: Require integration tests to execute an approved production harness
messages: Exercise the application through an approved integration-test harness.

nitpicker/naming-convention.description: Enforce naming conventions for everything across a codebase
messages: {{type}} name `{{name}}` must match one of the following formats: {{formats}}
{{type}} name `{{name}}` trimmed as `{{processedName}}` must match one of the following formats: {{formats}}
{{type}} name `{{name}}` must have one of the following {{position}}es: {{affixes}}
{{type}} name `{{name}}` must have {{count}} {{position}} underscore(s).
{{type}} name `{{name}}` must {{regexMatch}} the RegExp: {{regex}}
{{type}} name `{{name}}` must not have a {{position}} underscore.

nitpicker/no-assertion-in-loop.description: Ban assertions inside loops and iterating callbacks in a test
messages: This assertion sits in a `{{construct}}` whose body can run zero times (an empty collection, or a condition that is false at the start), so the test can pass without asserting anything. Assert the whole collection at once (`expect(orders).toEqual([...])`, `assert.deepStrictEqual(orders, [...])`), put a table of cases in a parameterized test (`it.each`/`test.each`, or node:test subtests registered from a literal table), or use the loop only to build data before an unconditional assertion. An exception fits only when the loop cannot be replaced by one of these, for example cases generated at run time.

This assertion runs once per row of a literal table in a `{{construct}}`: in Vitest, Jest and Mocha write the table as `it.each([...])('name', (row) => { ... })` (or `test.each`), so each row is its own test and a table that comes up empty cannot pass unnoticed; in node:test register one subtest per row (`for (const row of [...]) { await t.test(row.name, () => { ... }); }`). To check one collection instead, assert it whole (`expect(rows).toEqual([...])`). An exception fits only when the loop cannot be replaced by one of these, for example cases generated at run time.

These node:test subtests are registered in a `{{construct}}` over a collection that can be empty, so no case may run and the test can pass without asserting anything. Register them from a literal, non-empty table (`for (const row of [...]) { await t.test(row.name, () => { ... }); }`, or a same-file const holding that array), or assert the whole collection at once. An exception fits only when the loop cannot be replaced by one of these, for example cases generated at run time.

nitpicker/no-branch-in-composition-root.description: Keep branches out of composition roots, which only wire features together
messages: The composition root only wires features: it passes things in and does not branch, loop or default a missing value (`??`, `||`). Move this lookup or decision into the feature's adapters/ or domain/. A guard that only throws may stay: `const container = document.getElementById('root'); if (container === null) { throw new Error('#root is missing'); }` and then `createRoot(container)`. An exception fits only when this branch belongs here.

nitpicker/no-comments.description: Allow only non-suppression tool directives as comments, plus doc comments on exported API
messages: Fix the type error or narrow the value; TypeScript suppression comments ({{directive}}) are not allowed. To test that a type rejects a value, assert `expectTypeOf(fn).parameter(0).not.toExtend<Value>()`.
Fix the violation; inline ESLint disables are not allowed.
Test this code instead; coverage and mutation ignore comments ({{directive}}) hide untested code. An exception fits only when it truly cannot be tested.
Remove the comment and put the intent in code: a descriptive identifier, a named function, or a type. Only non-suppression tool directives may be comments.
JSDoc holds types only: remove the description text and put the intent in a descriptive identifier or a named function.
The JSDoc tag @{{tag}} is not allowed: JSDoc holds types only (@param, @returns, @type, @typedef, @template, @import).
Write the JSDoc tag as `{{usage}}`.
Do not use `any`, `*` or a bare `?` in a JSDoc type. Use `unknown` and parse it into a specific type at the boundary with zod, or write the specific type.
Use `undefined` for an absent value; `null` and the `?T` and `T?` forms are not allowed in a JSDoc type. Type it as optional with `undefined`.

Do not assert with a JSDoc cast (`/** @type {T} */ (value)`). Narrow the value (a discriminated union check or a zod parse) or give it the correct type at its source. `/** @type {const} */` is allowed.
This doc comment only restates {{name}}. Delete it, or say what the name cannot: a unit, a limit, an edge case or why.
This doc comment's description is {{lines}} lines (limit {{limit}}). Keep the non-obvious point, a unit, a limit or an edge case, and put the rest in names and types.
Doc comments are allowed only on exported declarations and the members of exported types. Remove this one and put the intent in code: a descriptive identifier, a named function, or a type.

nitpicker/no-compatibility-shim.description: Disallow deprecated declarations and second names for an exported API
messages: A `@deprecated` declaration keeps the old API next to its replacement. Delete it and update its callers to the replacement in the same change.
`{{ alias }}` is a second exported name for `{{ target }}`. Delete `{{ alias }}` and update its callers to import `{{ target }}`.

nitpicker/no-copy-pasted-tests.description: Require one it.each table instead of copies of a test
messages: This test repeats the body of {{count}} others and differs only in its literals. Write one `it.each` table with a row per case.

forms.message: Use a named export (`export function name() {}` or `export const name = ...`). Default exports are only allowed in config files, `declare module` blocks and the framework files that need one (Next.js routes, Storybook stories, Expo Router screens). An exception fits only when a framework or library requires it.

Use a named export (`export { name }`). Default exports are only allowed in config files and in the framework files that need one (Next.js routes, Storybook stories, Expo Router screens). An exception fits only when a framework or library requires it.

nitpicker/no-default-export.description: Disallow default exports outside config files

nitpicker/no-dev-dependency-in-productio.description: Production code imports only packages listed in dependencies
messages: {{name}} is only a devDependency, but production code imports it. Move it to "dependencies" in package.json. {{hint}}
{{manifest}} is not a JSON object, so imports cannot be checked against its dependencies. Fix the file.

nitpicker/no-disabled-tls-verification.description: Disallow turning off TLS certificate verification
messages: Turning off TLS certificate verification lets anyone on the network pose as the server, and turning it off by environment ships the switch to production. Keep verification on in every environment and trust the certificate authority instead: `new https.Agent({ ca: readFileSync(caPath) })`, `tlsCAFile` for MongoDB, or set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS for a private CA; for browser automation against a local certificate pin it with `--ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list=<hash>`. A server that asks for optional client certificates sets `requestCert: true` and checks `socket.authorized`. An exception fits only when a contained case cannot do that.

nitpicker/no-falsy-default.description: Disallow replacing a falsy parameter with a default through || or a ternary
messages: `{{ name }}` is replaced by the default whenever it is falsy, so `0`, `''` and `false` count as not given. Default only `undefined` with `??` (`limit ?? DEFAULT_LIMIT`), or test `limit === undefined`.

"{{name}}" is memoized lazily at module level and filled by a call, so whichever test runs first pays for its setup, reports show that test as slow, and test order starts to matter. Compute it once in beforeAll and let tests read it. An exception fits only when the setup is cheap or the lazy memo is intended.
Fixed sleeps are non-deterministic; wait on a condition with vi.waitFor or expect.poll. An exception fits only when a real wait is unavoidable.

Do not assert absence by letting a wait time out: `.rejects` passes only after the full timeout, so the test is slow and depends on the delay. Advance fake timers past the delay (`vi.advanceTimersByTime`) and assert absence at once, such as `expect(screen.queryByRole('tooltip')).toBeNull()`. An exception fits only when a real wait is unavoidable.
`waitForTimeout` sleeps on wall-clock time. Wait on a condition instead, such as `await expect(locator).toBeVisible()`. An exception fits only when a real wait is unavoidable.

`cy.wait(<number>)` sleeps on wall-clock time. Wait on a request alias (`cy.wait('@request')`) or retry an assertion (`cy.get(selector).should('be.visible')`). An exception fits only when a real wait is unavoidable.

nitpicker/no-forwarding-wrapper.description: Disallow a function that only forwards its parameters to another function
messages: `{{ name }}` only forwards its parameters to `{{ target }}` and has the same parameter and return types. Delete it and export `{{ target }}` in its place with `export { {{ target }} as {{ exported }} }`, or call `{{ target }}` directly.
`{{ name }}` only forwards its parameters to `{{ target }}` and has the same parameter and return types. Call `{{ target }}` directly where `{{ name }}` is used and delete the wrapper.
Do not create a git repository in each test or beforeEach. Build a template repository once in beforeAll and copy it per test with cpSync.

nitpicker/no-handwritten-boundary-guard.description: Require external data in adapters to be parsed with a schema instead of a hand-written type guard
messages: Do not hand-write a type guard for unknown input: parse it once at the boundary with {{phrase}} ({{example}}). A predicate over a union (`(result): result is Ok => result.kind === "ok"`) is fine. An exception fits only when the guard is genuinely needed.

Do not hand-narrow an `unknown` value with `typeof x === "object"` or `"key" in x`: parse it once at the boundary with {{phrase}} ({{example}}). A caught error is read with `error instanceof Error`. An exception fits only when the narrowing is genuinely needed.

This overload implementation returns unknown or any, which makes its overload signatures a cast. Return a typed value, or split it into separate functions. An exception fits only when it is deliberate.
Pass `JSON.parse(text)` straight into `{{call}}(...)` inside the same `try`. An exception fits only when the text is trusted and already typed.
Copy a value with `structuredClone(value)`, not `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value))`. An exception fits only when it is deliberate.
Inject the dependency instead of replacing internal production module {{source}}. An exception fits only when injection is not possible.
Inject the dependency instead of replacing a function of internal production module {{source}} with `vi.spyOn`. An exception fits only when injection is not possible.
Prefer vi.waitFor / expect.poll over setInterval polling in tests.
Number constants declarations must use 'const'.

No magic number: {{raw}}. Name it with a module-level constant: `const SECONDS_PER_DAY = 24 * 60 * 60;` (-1, 0, 1, 2, 10, 100 and 1000, an HTTP status code such as `res.status(404)` and the digits of `toFixed(2)` are allowed). An exception fits only when the number is clear where it is.

nitpicker/no-managed-resource-constructi.description: Keep managed resource construction in approved composition roots
messages: Construct {{name}} only in the composition root (src/main/composition-root.ts, main.ts or server.ts) and pass it in as a parameter. An exception fits only when it is a plain value, not a long-lived resource.

nitpicker/no-mocking-subject-under-test.description: Prevent a test from mocking the production module it imports as its subject
messages: Do not mock the production subject {{source}}.

nitpicker/no-module-level-let.description: Ban module-level let, which is hidden mutable module state
messages: Use 'const' instead of module-level 'let'. Keep state in a parameter or in an object constructed in the composition root and passed in.

nitpicker/no-module-level-mutable-state.description: Disallow module-level collections and objects that the module mutates
messages: Module-level '{{name}}' is mutated, which is hidden shared state. Build a lookup table inside a function and return it, create shared state in the composition root and pass it in, or return a new value instead of mutating. An exception fits only when it is a deliberate per-process singleton.

Module-level '{{name}}' is an exported mutable collection that any importer can change. If importers only read it, annotate it with a readonly type (`ReadonlySet<T>`, `ReadonlyMap<K, V>`, `readonly number[]`); otherwise build it inside a function and return it, or create it in the composition root and pass it in. An exception fits only when it is a deliberate per-process singleton.

nitpicker/no-mutating-method-in-domain.description: Disallow mutating methods of arrays, Set, Map, Date, typed arrays, Buffer and URLSearchParams in domain code
messages: domain/ code does not mutate values, and {{owner}}.{{method}} changes the value it is called on: build a new value instead, e.g. new Set([...set, x]), new Map([...map, [key, value]]), new Map(xs.map((x) => [x.id, x] as const)) or new Date(ms + delta).

Do not start a Node process (process.execPath, node, npx or a node_modules/.bin script) from a test or beforeEach. Import the function and call it in-process; start the application as a process only through the AppProcess harness in the test fixtures. An exception fits only when this test checks the process boundary itself (exit codes, signals, stdout).

forms.message: Use `undefined` for an absent value, and an optional field or parameter (`value?: T`) where it may be missing. `null` is only for strict comparison with a library value and the `JSON.stringify` replacer argument. An exception fits only when a framework or library requires it.

nitpicker/no-null.description: Disallow null outside the allowed library forms

nitpicker/no-parameter-mutation.description: Disallow changing an array, Set, Map or indexed object that a parameter holds in place
messages: `{{ name }}` changes the value the caller passed in. Build and return a new value instead (`[...items, item]`, `new Set([...set, item])`, `{ ...table, [key]: value }`, `items.toSorted()`), or copy the parameter first (`const copy = [...items]`).

nitpicker/no-partial-output-assertion.description: Require tests to assert the whole output instead of a fragment of it
messages: Assert the whole output with `toEqual` or `toBe` instead of checking that it contains a fragment (`toContain`, or `toMatch` with a pattern that is not anchored `^...$`): a fragment passes even when the rest is wrong. An exception fits only when the output is too large or unordered to pin.

Pass the whole expected value to `toEqual` instead of a partial match (`toMatchObject`, `expect.objectContaining`, `expect.stringContaining`, `expect.arrayContaining`): the rest of the value goes unchecked. Use `expect.any(Type)` for a field that varies. An exception fits only when the value is too large or unordered to pin.

nitpicker/no-process-access-outside-comp.description: Read environment variables and exit the process only in the composition root
messages: Read environment variables only in the composition root: parse the environment once with a zod schema there and pass the typed config down as a parameter. An exception fits only when this module is a config loader or a script.

process.exit stops the whole process from inside library code. Return a result or throw an Error subclass, and call process.exit only in the composition root or a main guard (`if (import.meta.main)`). An exception fits only when this module is an entry script.

A test helper or fixture script may use process.{{member}} only inside a main guard such as `if (import.meta.main)`. Export a function that takes the arguments and returns the exit code, and call it from the main guard, so tests can import it instead of spawning it.

nitpicker/no-production-console.description: Keep production logging on the application logger path
messages: Use the application logger instead of console.{{method}}(). An exception fits only when this module prints the program output.
Use the application logger instead of process.{{stream}}.write(). Program output is written in the composition root. An exception fits only when this module prints the program output.

forms.message: Use async/await (with try/catch) instead of promise chains, and Promise.all with a limiter for concurrent work. An exception fits only when a framework or library requires it.

nitpicker/no-promise-chain.description: Disallow then, catch and finally promise chains

messages: Keep the {{kind}} timeout between 1 and {{ceiling}} ms for this test project. Make the test faster or configure its named project timeout in tools.tests.timeouts.
Give the {{kind}} timeout as a number between 1 and {{ceiling}} ms written in this file, or keep the default.

nitpicker/no-real-time-random-or-network.description: Keep the real clock, randomness and network out of tests
messages: The real clock makes the test depend on when it runs. Pass the time in, or fake it with `vi.useFakeTimers()` and `vi.setSystemTime(...)`.
Real randomness makes the test fail on some runs. Pass a seeded or fixed value in, or fix it with `vi.spyOn(Math, "random")`.
A unit test must not reach the network. Inject the client and fake it.

nitpicker/no-self-recursion.description: Disallow a function that calls itself, directly or through another function
messages: '{{name}}' calls itself. Retry or poll: loop with for...of over attempt numbers. Tree walk (directories, AST, JSON): for...of over a worklist, pushing each node's children onto it (for (const node of pending) { pending.push(...children) }). Flat data: map, filter, flatMap or Object.fromEntries. A component that renders itself in JSX is not reported. An exception fits only when the recursion is bounded and deliberate.

'{{name}}' calls itself. domain/ has no loops and no recursion, so a walk over data of unknown depth (a tree) belongs in adapters/: for...of over a worklist, pushing each node's children onto it. Pass domain/ the flat result; flat data uses map, filter, flatMap or Object.fromEntries. An exception fits only when the recursion is bounded and deliberate.

'{{name}}' and '{{other}}' call each other. Replace the cycle with a for...of loop over a worklist, or merge them into one function that loops. An exception fits only when the recursion is bounded and deliberate.

Do not start a server or worker thread in each test or beforeEach. Start it once in beforeAll and reset its state between tests, or test the logic against an in-memory implementation and keep the real transport for transport tests. An exception fits only when each test needs a fresh server.

nitpicker/no-shared-test-state.description: Ban initialised let state shared by the tests of a file
messages: Shared mutable state makes tests depend on their order. Keep `{{name}}` inside the test, or declare it without a value and set it in `beforeEach`.

nitpicker/no-shell-string-command.description: Disallow running a shell command built from a string
messages: A shell command built from a variable or template is a command injection risk. Run the program with `execFile(program, [args])` or `spawn(program, [args])`, one argument per array entry. If the command is fixed and trusted, write it as a plain string literal.

`{{program}} {{flag}}` runs a command built from a variable or template through a shell, a command injection risk like `exec`. Run the program itself with `execFile(program, [args])`, one argument per array entry. If the command is fixed and trusted, write it as a plain string literal.

nitpicker/no-silent-catch.description: Require a catch clause to use the caught value or return a failure result, not discard it
messages: This catch discards the failure. Return a failure result (`return { kind: 'malformed-json' }`), or rethrow an Error subclass with `{ cause: error }`. An exception fits only when dropping it is intended.

nitpicker/no-sql-string-building.description: Disallow SQL text built from runtime values
messages: SQL text built by {{kind}} lets a runtime value change the statement (SQL injection). Use {{tagged}}bind parameters: `pool.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1", [id])` (pg), `?` with an array (mysql2, sqlite, knex.raw, knex.whereRaw), `:name` (sequelize, typeorm `.where("user.id = :id", { id })`). Placeholder lists are built from placeholders alone: `ids.map(() => "?").join(",")`, rows as `rows.map(() => "(?, ?)").join(", ")`, `$${i + 1}`, and optional filters as `conditions.push("name = ?")` joined with `" AND "`. A table or column name comes from a fixed lookup (`const COLUMNS = { name: "name" } as const; COLUMNS[key]`) or a value typed as a union of literal names (`table: "users" | "orders"`). An exception fits only when the value is trusted and cannot be written that way.

nitpicker/no-switched-off-tests.description: Ban test forms that switch a test off
messages: Do not leave a `todo` test: write the test, or delete the stub.
A literal condition switches the test off for good. Delete the test or make it run; a real platform condition such as `process.platform === "win32"` is allowed.

nitpicker/no-test-helpers-in-source.description: Keep test helpers and fixtures out of production source roots
messages: This looks like a test helper ({{name}}), but it sits in production source, so it is mutation-tested and shipped. Tests in this project live under {{testRoot}}/, so move it to a test-support/ folder there ({{testRoot}}/test-support/). An exception fits only when it is real production code.

This looks like a test helper ({{name}}), but it sits in production source outside a test-support/ folder. Tests in this project sit next to the code, and test-only modules go in a test-support/ folder beside the code they serve: move it there. An exception fits only when it is real production code.
Remove the retry: a test that passes on a later attempt hides a flaky or racy test. Fix the cause, such as waiting on the condition instead of a delay or isolating shared state.

nitpicker/no-throw.description: Disallow throw so expected failures are returned as discriminated unions
messages: Return a discriminated-union failure result (for example { kind: "failed", reason }) instead of throwing.

nitpicker/no-tri-state-boolean.description: Disallow a boolean that can also be undefined or null
messages: {{ name }} is a boolean that can also be absent, so it has three states: true, false and nothing. Take a required `boolean`, or name each state in a union of string literals (`'on' | 'off' | 'auto'`).

nitpicker/no-ui-framework-in-domain.description: Keep UI frameworks and UI state libraries out of domain/
messages: domain/ does not import a UI framework or UI state library (`{{source}}`): components, hooks and stores live in adapters/ (or shared/ui) and call the logic in domain/, which takes and returns plain values. An exception fits only when a framework requires this file in domain/.

domain/ does not render: JSX belongs to a component in adapters/ (or shared/ui), which calls the logic in domain/ and renders its plain result. An exception fits only when a framework requires this file in domain/.

domain/ does not import a UI framework or UI state library, here `{{framework}}` through `{{source}}`: components, hooks and stores live in adapters/ (or shared/ui) and call the logic in domain/, which takes and returns plain values. An exception fits only when a framework requires this file in domain/.

nitpicker/no-uncollected-tests.description: Report test calls in a file the test runner never collects
messages: This file defines tests but is not named like a test file, so they never run. Rename it `*.test.ts` (or `*.spec.ts`). An exception fits only when another test file runs it on purpose.

{{timer}} waits {{name}} ({{value}} ms), a module constant that exported "{{owner}}" cannot override, so a test must wait it out or fake timers. Accept the delay as an option with {{name}} as its default, for example "{ delayMs = {{name}} } = {}". An exception fits only when the delay is deliberately fixed.

nitpicker/no-unknown-in-domain.description: Disallow the unknown type in parameter and property types of domain code
messages: domain/ code takes typed values, not unknown (also through a type alias). Write a readonly type for this value in domain/; adapters/ parses the input with {{phrase}} and passes the result in (the parsed value is assignable to a readonly type; do not import the schema type from adapters/). A caught error may be typed unknown as `cause` or `error`. An exception fits only when the value is genuinely opaque.

nitpicker/no-unknown-main-folder.description: Allow only features, shared and the composition root under src/main
messages: '{{folder}}' sits directly in src/main/, which holds only features/, shared/ and the composition root (composition-root.ts, main.ts, server.ts) and index.ts. Move it into the feature that uses it, or into shared/ when several features need it. An exception fits only when the file is deliberate.

'{{folder}}/' is not a layer of this layout. Under src/main/ put code in features/<name>/ (domain/ for pure logic, adapters/ for I/O), in shared/ when several features need it, or in the composition root. An exception fits only when this folder is deliberate.

'{{folder}}/' is not a layer of a feature. A feature holds domain/ for pure logic and adapters/ for I/O (and ui/ for components in a React project), and its public index.ts. An exception fits only when this folder is deliberate.

'{{folder}}' sits directly in a feature folder, which holds only its public index.ts besides domain/ and adapters/ (and ui/ for components in a React project). Move it into domain/ if it is pure logic or adapters/ if it does I/O. An exception fits only when the file is deliberate.

nitpicker/no-unowned-async-assertion.description: Require tests to wait for the callbacks that hold their assertions
messages: This assertion runs in a `{{host}}` callback the test does not wait for: the test function returns first, so a failure is lost or blamed on another test. Await a promise the callback resolves, or fake the timers and advance them past it in the test. An exception fits only when the test waits for the callback in a way nitpicker cannot see.

This assertion runs in a `{{host}}` callback the test does not wait for: the test function returns first, so a failure is lost or blamed on another test. Await a promise the callback resolves, or `await` after scheduling it so it runs before the test ends. An exception fits only when the test waits for the callback in a way nitpicker cannot see.

This assertion runs in a `{{host}}` handler, and nothing after it in the test triggers the event or waits for it, so the event can arrive after the test has finished and a failure is lost or blamed on another test. Trigger the event in the test after adding the handler, or await it (`await once(emitter, 'ready')`, or a promise the handler resolves). An exception fits only when the test waits for the callback in a way nitpicker cannot see.

This assertion runs in the callback of `{{host}}`, which Node calls after the test function returns, so a failure is lost or blamed on another test. Await the promise form of the API (`node:fs/promises`, `util.promisify`) instead. An exception fits only when the test waits for the callback in a way nitpicker cannot see.

nitpicker/no-unsafe-deserialization.description: Disallow rebuilding code or objects from untrusted data
messages: `{{name}}` rebuilds functions from the data it reads, so a crafted payload runs code. Read the data as JSON, `JSON.parse(text)`, and check it against a schema (zod, valibot) into a typed value. An exception fits only when this process alone writes and reads the data.

`v8.deserialize(v8.serialize(value))` copies a value through the structured-clone bytes. Copy it with `structuredClone(value)`, which keeps `Map`, `Set`, `Date` and cycles and parses no bytes. An exception fits only when you need the v8 wire format here.

`yaml.{{name}}` in js-yaml 3 loads with `DEFAULT_FULL_SCHEMA`, so `!!js/function` tags build functions from the text.
